answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids, and slash that stake when an independent audit confirms fabricated work. The rule does not prove that one person controls only one account; instead, it makes influence costly: splitting capital across sybils leaves less stake behind each bid and risks losing every deposit. Even an island of colluding agents must fund its own exposure, while a meadow of honest agents can report suspicious output; yarrow may mark one audited task, not establish identity.
